title: Key features of graphs
keyIdea: Read a graph's story from its features: intercepts, where it rises or falls, its highest and lowest points, symmetry and end behaviour.

kid: A graph tells a story. Going up means getting bigger. Going down means getting smaller.
The top of a hill is a maximum. The bottom of a valley is a minimum. Where the graph crosses an axis is an intercept.
adult: Increasing means y rises as x moves right, so the tangent slopes up. Decreasing means it slopes down. At a maximum or minimum, the tangent is flat.
The y-intercept is where x = 0. The x-intercepts are the zeros. Symmetry and end behaviour describe the overall shape, such as a parabola that rises at both ends.

familyTip: Look at a weather app's temperature graph. When was it warmest? When was it rising?
